summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted less than 24 hours after discharge due to sudden, severe right hip pain. He has a complex history including end-stage renal disease, recent MRSA line infection, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, and avascular necrosis of the right femoral head. Imaging confirmed advanced avascular necrosis with joint collapse and effusion, raising concern for possible infection. A fluoroscopic-guided hip aspiration was performed, yielding 0.5 mL of fluid. Gram stain showed no organisms, and cultures remained negative, ruling out septic arthritis. Pain was controlled with oxycodone, and vancomycin was discontinued after completion of therapy for prior MRSA infection. The patient was discharged home with services, advised to follow up with orthopedics for evaluation of hip replacement, and given updated medication instructions.
